original_scope: Low angular spiral with a wide umbilical recess. Genus-level fossil-form interpretation based on E. pentangulatus; not a single specimen facsimile.

reference_anchor.primary_photos: Fryda, Nutzel & Wagner2008 Paleozoic Gastropoda Fig10.5 B,C ONLY. E.pentangulatus, Carboniferous. Side and upper-oblique views show low angular whorl, broad depressed coil and mineral-filled terminal face. Do not use A (Schizostoma), D-F (Macluritella), G orH.
reference_anchor.museum_photos: Ghedoghedo, Teylers Museum53.jpg and Verona7.jpg, labelled E.pentangulatus on Commons. Support broad shallow coil and low irregular fossil form. No scale supplied for these individuals.

reference_anchor.era_correction: OriginalDevonian is a representative planning interval. Selected E.pentangulatus is Carboniferous; retain original field privately and set finalmetadata Carboniferous. Root approved same-genus correction21:42.

scale.basis: English inch25.4mm; line assumed1/12inch. Rounded working dimensions51mm wide,19mm high,17mm lastwhorl. Historical species-description values, not a calibrated individual reconstruction.
scale.tolerance: Approximately +/-10% simplification; avoid false precision. In-plane second diameter about45–51mm inferred from photographs, not independently measured.

morphology: Low discoidal shell, about five progressively enlarging whorls; large outer whorl and broad depressed centre, NOT a tall snail tower, ammonite septate disk, simple torus or detached spring.

Upper whorl has flat-to-gently sloping inner shelf meeting a distinct blunt angular shoulder, with convex outer wall. Basal surface convex with an obtuse secondary angulation. Strong stepped/near-polygonal cross-section must survive low-poly simplification.

Wide umbilical recess exposes inner winding; it is a shallow-to-moderate open depression bounded by coiled shell, not an arbitrarily drilled cylindrical through-hole. Fine early coil may close at centre.

Keep upper outline and coiling direction of FigC unmirrored. Slightly raised/depressed centre and low overall height; do not derive left/right chirality solely from an unlabeled opposite-side photograph.

Final cross-section in FigB is mineral-filled and irregularly subrounded/polygonal, not an intact hollow aperture. Preserve a distinct terminal face and subdued surviving edge, no deep tunnel, extended siphonal canal or flaring trumpet.

Growth lines are fine, shallow and gently curved across shoulder; no giant axial ribs, spikes, cowry teeth, sutures or living tissue. No matrix slab, mounting material, museum numbers or printed labels.
uncertainty: Scale and shape are from different published material; explicitly disclose genus-level interpretation, not single-specimen measured replica.
No direct basal photograph of the same FigB/C fossil; base and umbilical depth are conservatively inferred from M’Coy description. A basal QA render is required to expose this interpretation.
Fine apertural lip and missing surface cannot be restored as pristine anatomy. Fossil termination remains mineral-filled.
Euomphalus sometimes treated historically as subgenus of Straparollus; target is type species E.pentangulatus, not substituted S.northi. No soft anatomy or higher phylogenetic claims.
palette: Matte neutral warm grey stone, slight terminal-fill variation; no photographic textures.
acceptance_focus: Front: low shell height, integrated angular upper shoulder, filled terminal face facing camera.
Side: about19mmheight for51mmdiameter, no elevated tower; convex outerwall and blunt basal angulation.
Top: broad exposed spiral and depressed centre match FigC without mirroring or radial symmetry.
Perspective: continuous coiling, proper angular whorl transition, no separate rings or invented hollow aperture.
Basal extra: wide shallow umbilical depression, inner coil readable, no arbitrary cylindrical drilled hole.
Four template views plus one justified basal view; two isolated deterministic rebuilds and fixed localdependencies. Prep is not QA/modelPASS.
